name: Fretebras
tagline: Brazilian freight marketplace where shippers and agents post truck loads and carriers and owner-operators find return hauls.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Plans differ for drivers versus freight posters and are quoted on the site.

verdictSummary: The software here is a search form over a list of loads, which an agent can produce before lunch. The product is the fact that tens of thousands of Brazilian loads get posted to it every day and hundreds of thousands of drivers check it, which no amount of code gives you. A load board with no loads is a spreadsheet with extra steps, and the first time you post your own freight to it you will discover the problem. There is also the unglamorous layer: CNPJ and ANTT checks, document verification, fraud and cargo-theft screening, dispute handling. Build the private version if you run a fleet and want your own dispatch ledger, not if you want a market.
coreLoopDIY: A private load board for one fleet or broker: post loads with origin, destination, cargo type, weight and price, let a known list of drivers claim them from their phone, and track status from offered to delivered.
requirements: Node 20 and a machine or small VPS to run it on
Your own list of drivers or shippers, since there is no supply to borrow
Optional: a geocoding key if you want distance and route math instead of plain text city fields
Optional: WhatsApp or SMS gateway credentials if you want claim notifications
whatYouLose: Liquidity: the daily flood of posted loads and the drivers watching for them
Carrier and driver vetting: document checks, CNPJ and ANTT status, fraud and theft screening
Mobile apps with push alerts, which is how drivers actually use this at a truck stop
Risk and payment infrastructure: insurance partners, freight payment tooling, dispute mediation
Brand recognition that makes a stranger in another state willing to pick up your cargo
moatNotes: Classic two-sided board with a cold start that is geographic as well as numeric: you need density on specific lanes, not just totals.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because an empty return trip costs real money and this is the cheapest place to avoid one. A carrier pays a subscription that is small relative to one deadhead leg, and a shipper pays to reach trucks it has no relationship with. Both sides are buying strangers, which is exactly the thing software cannot manufacture. The dry version: nobody subscribes for the UI, they subscribe because the other side of the market is already logged in.
notes: The board is a weekend build; the traffic on it is not. The moat is marketplace liquidity on thousands of Brazilian lanes, plus the verification layer that makes strangers trust each other with a truckload of cargo.
prompt:
Build a private freight dispatch board for a single carrier or broker. Not a public marketplace: a closed board where a known set of drivers claims loads from a known set of shippers.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Drizzle for schema and migrations. Runs locally with npm run dev and on one small VPS with npm run build and npm start. No external SaaS, no analytics, no telemetry.

Data model:
- users: id, name, phone, role one of dispatcher or driver, invite_code, created_at
- loads: id, origin_city, origin_state, dest_city, dest_state, cargo_type, weight_kg, vehicle_type, pickup_date, price_brl, notes, status one of open, claimed, loaded, delivered, cancelled, posted_by, claimed_by, created_at
- load_events: id, load_id, user_id, from_status, to_status, note, created_at

Auth: phone number plus invite code, session in an httpOnly cookie signed with SESSION_SECRET from .env. No OAuth, no email, no password reset flow. Dispatchers create invite codes.

Screens:
- Driver view, mobile first: list of open loads filterable by origin state, destination state and vehicle type, sorted by pickup date. One tap to claim. A My Loads page with buttons to advance status and add a note.
- Dispatcher view: form to post a load, table of all loads with status filters, full event timeline per load, ability to unclaim or cancel.

In scope: a /api/loads GET endpoint returning open loads as JSON, Brazilian formatting for currency and dates, a seed script that inserts two dispatchers, five drivers and fifteen loads across realistic lanes.

Out of scope, do not build: payments, document or ANTT verification, mobile native apps, push notifications, maps or route optimisation, public signup, chat. Put TODO comments where WhatsApp notifications would hook in.

Deliver a README with setup steps, the .env keys needed, and one honest paragraph stating that this is a dispatch ledger for an existing network and has no load supply of its own.
